structure: COLD OPEN (cut letters, the mass) -> the boon -> two years -> Kunti's son -> the forced birth (close-up) -> the iron mass -> Vyasa (gold) -> a rest -> TURN + SIGNATURE: fold, cut, unfold into 101 -> the pots, Duryodhana -> the omens (the gong) -> a rest -> the king refuses -> PAYOFF: a hundred and one daughter -> end card.

names.Kunti: wife of Pandu, the king's brother

loop.hookQuestion: How does one lump of flesh become a hundred sons?

strings.sourceLine: Text: the Mahabharata · BORI Critical Edition

lines.text: One lump of flesh. A hundred sons.
lines.note: COLD OPEN, sound and motion from frame 0: on deep indigo paper the red mass sits in a lotus of cut paper and beats like a heart; the hook is cut-out cream letters ONE LUMP OF FLESH / A HUNDRED SONS popping in on 12 fps steps, the second line on "hundred". CE 1.107.12, 1.107.8.

lines.text: Gandhari cared for a weary sage, who granted her one hundred sons.
lines.note: Rice paper: Vyasa (deep plum-black paper, matted hair, beard) on the left, Gandhari (red, cream blindfold) bowing on the right; between them a cut lotus with a hundred tiny petals unfolds on "hundred". CE 1.107.7-8.

lines.text: She carried the child two years.
lines.note: Jade-green night: Gandhari seated in profile; paper moons step across a jali window behind her, crescent by crescent (24 phases). CE 1.107.9.

lines.text: Then her sister-in-law bore a son, bright as the morning sun.
lines.note: Turmeric paper: an 8-fold sun rosette (one wedge mirrored) rises behind a far pavilion where Kunti holds a child; Gandhari in the near layer hears it, head turned. CE 1.107.10, 1.107.15.

lines.text: In grief, without telling her husband, she forced the birth.
lines.note: Violet-black paper, a close profile of Gandhari (blindfold, a tear crescent), the face piece swaps from still to grief; the blind king far off behind a jali, unaware. Restraint: no blow shown; her hands press, the paper shudders. CE 1.107.11.

lines.text: Out came a mass of flesh, hard as iron.
lines.note: Iron-black paper: the red mass drops into frame (cardboard thud, camera shake), cut with crescent rivets like a ball of iron. CE 1.107.12.

lines.text: That sage, Vyasa, came: "Fill a hundred pots with ghee. Sprinkle it with cold water."
lines.note: Rice paper: Vyasa arrives in the only GOLD FOIL of the film (a gold halo rosette, 8-fold), stands over the mass; cut water drops fall on it. CE 1.107.13, 1.107.17-18.

lines.text: It split into a hundred and one parts, each the size of a thumb joint.
lines.note: TURN · SIGNATURE: the rest (a 3.5 dB dip, 1.6 s, filled by the paper) is the fold and the cut: on indigo the mass flattens into a red sheet, folds three times (swish, crease tap), scissors cut (shear sweeps); the voice comes in over the cutting and the sheet UNFOLDS with three snaps on "hundred" into 101 pieces (1 + 4 + 8 + 16 + 32 + 40). CE 1.107.19-20.

lines.text: Each went into its pot. Duryodhana was born first.
lines.note: HOLES ARE LIGHT: rows of 101 jali pots backlit on night paper; one pot cracks open and a red infant piece stands up. CE 1.107.21-22, 1.107.24.

lines.text: Jackals howled. The brahmins said: give this one up.
lines.note: Violet-black night paper: cut-out jackals howl in a circle round the palace (the ONE big ghanta stroke on "Jackals"); the brahmins point at the child. CE 1.107.28-31.

lines.text: For love of his son, the king would not.
lines.note: Rice paper, a rest before it (a dip): the blind king (crowned, eyes closed crescents) holds the child to his chest and turns away from the brahmins. CE 1.107.33.

lines.text: Within a month all hundred were born, then one daughter: Duhshala.
lines.note: PAYOFF: symmetry replicates: a hundred small red boys in rings round one girl piece at the centre, the camera pulling back to the whole window-flower. CE 1.107.34, 1.107.37.
END CARD: MAHABHARATAM / AS VYASA TOLD IT cut letters on a red banner, FOLLOW, the source line. Nothing about how it was made.
